source.title: Some open problems in computational algebraic geometry

accepted.question_text: Let C be a genus-2 curve over C that admits a maximal degree-7 map psi_1: C -> E_1 to an elliptic curve, so that its Jacobian J_C is (7,7)-isogenous to E_1 x E_2 for a second degree-7 elliptic subcover E_2 and belongs to the locus L_7 in M_2 of genus-2 curves with (7,7)-split Jacobian. Determine the locus L_7 in the moduli space M_2 of genus-2 curves, and determine the relation between the elliptic curves E_1 and E_2 in each case.

evidence.quote: For our purposes, Ln will simply be the locus of genus 2 curves whose Jacobian is (n, n)-isogenous to a product of two elliptic curves.
Problem 1. Determine the locus Ln in M2 for n = 7. Further, determine the relation between the elliptic curves E1 and E2 in each case.

accepted.question_text: Let C be a genus-2 curve over C whose Jacobian is (n,n)-isogenous to a product E_1 x E_2 of elliptic curves, and let L_n be the corresponding locus in the moduli space M_2 of genus-2 curves. For the even degrees n=4 and n=6, determine the loci L_4 and L_6 in M_2 and determine the relation between the elliptic curves E_1 and E_2 in each case.
accepted.context_brief: Even-degree split Jacobian loci in M_2

evidence.quote: For our purposes, Ln will simply be the locus of genus 2 curves whose Jacobian is (n, n)-isogenous to a product of two elliptic curves.
Problem 3. Determine the loci Ln in M2 for n = 4, 6. Further, determine the relation between the elliptic curves E1 and E2 in each case.

accepted.question_text: Over the complex numbers, for each genus g <= 10 and each finite group G that occurs as the full automorphism group of genus-g algebraic curves, determine all inclusion relations among the loci M(g,G) in the moduli space M_g, where M(g,G) denotes the locus of genus-g curves whose automorphism group is G.

evidence.quote: M(g, H) (locus of curves in Mg with automorphism group H) is a sublocus of M(g, G).
Problem 4. Determine the inclusion among the loci M(g, G) for algebraic curves defined over C and genus g <= 10.

accepted.question_text: For every genus g <= 48, determine the inclusion relations among the automorphism-group and signature loci of genus-g algebraic curves in the moduli space M_g.
accepted.context_brief: Inclusions among loci up to genus 48

evidence.quote: In the above diagram are given inclusions among the loci of genus 4 curves.
Problem 5. Determine the inclusions among the loci for all g <= 48

accepted.question_text: Given a finite group G and a signature sigma such that G occurs as the automorphism group of some genus-g algebraic curve with that signature, find explicit algebraic equations for the corresponding curve or family of curves.
accepted.context_brief: Equations for curves with prescribed automorphism data

evidence.quote: Problem 6. For any group G and a given signature σ such that G occurs as automorphism group of some genus g curve, find the corresponding equation for the curve.
Such problem is open even for small genus.

accepted.question_text: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, a Hurwitz curve of genus g is a curve with exactly 84(g-1) automorphisms. Compute explicit equations for the Hurwitz curves of genus 14, and if possible for the Hurwitz curves of genus 17.
accepted.context_brief: Equations for Hurwitz curves of genus 14 and 17

evidence.quote: A Hurwitz curve is a genus g curve, defined over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, which has 84(g - 1) automorphisms.
Problem 7. Compute equations for the Hurwitz curves of genus 14, and possibly 17.

accepted.question_text: For algebraic curves of genus g <= 10 over fields of positive characteristic, determine the complete list of finite groups that occur as full automorphism groups.

evidence.quote: Let X denote a smooth, genus g algebraic curve defined over k, char k = p > 0.
Problem 8. Determine the list of groups which occur as full automorphism groups for genus g <= 10 algebraic curves defined over a field of positive characteristic.

accepted.question_text: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 0, and let X_g be a cyclic curve with function field K=k(x,y) given by y^n=f(x), so that k(x) is a degree-n genus-zero subfield and C_n=Gal(K/k(x)) is normal in Aut(K/k). Determine all finite groups that occur as full automorphism groups of such cyclic curves.
accepted.context_brief: Full automorphism groups of cyclic curves

evidence.quote: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p and Xg be a genus g cyclic curve defined over k and given by the equation y n = f(x).
Problem 9. Determine the list of groups that occur as full automorphism groups of cyclic curves defined over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 0.

accepted.question_text: Let X be an algebraic curve of genus g <= 48 with automorphism group G=Aut(X). Using the subgroup structure of G and the quotient curves X/H, determine all possible isogeny decompositions of the Jacobian Jac(X), especially decompositions into products of Jacobians of quotient curves.

evidence.quote: Let X be a genus g algebraic curve with automorphism group G := Aut (X ).
Problem 10. Using the structure of automorphism groups of algebraic curves of genus g <= 48, determine possible decompositions of Jacobians for these curves.

accepted.question_text: Determine all algebraic curves of genus g <= 10 whose Jacobian is isogenous to a product of elliptic curves.

evidence.quote: Problem 13. Determine all algebraic curves of genus g <= 10 such that their Jacobian splits into a product of elliptic curves.

accepted.question_text: Find a system of invariants that classifies isomorphism classes of genus-3 hyperelliptic curves, equivalently a set of invariants that separates points of the genus-3 hyperelliptic moduli space.

evidence.quote: In other words, there is no known way of identifying isomorphism classes of hyperelliptic curves of genus g >= 3.
Problem 14. Find invariants which classify the isomorphism classes of genus 3 hyperelliptic curves.

accepted.question_text: Determine the invariant theory of binary octavics: compute the ring of invariants of homogeneous degree-8 binary forms over C, including correct generators and algebraic relations.
accepted.context_brief: Ring of invariants of binary octavics

evidence.quote: Denote by S(n, r) the graded ring of invariants of homogeneous polynomials of order r in n variables over C.
Problem 15. Determine the ring of invariants of binary octavics.

accepted.question_text: For cyclic algebraic curves that form positive-dimensional loci in the moduli space M_g, define invariants analogous to the dihedral invariants used for hyperelliptic curves with extra involutions, and use them to describe the corresponding cyclic moduli.

evidence.quote: We call such invariants dihedral invariants of hyperelliptic curves.
Problem 16. Define similar invariants for all cases of cyclic curves which correspond to higher dimension locus in the moduli Mg.

accepted.question_text: Determine the algebraic relations among the dihedral invariants on every sublocus of the cyclic moduli of algebraic curves.

evidence.quote: We call such invariants dihedral invariants of hyperelliptic curves.
Problem 17. Determine algebraic relations among "dihedral" invariants for all subloci of the "cyclic" moduli.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a smooth projective complex curve of genus g >= 3, let G be a finite group acting faithfully on X, and let sigma be the signature of the G-action. Describe the locus M_g(G,sigma) of curves in the genus-g moduli space M_g with automorphism group/action data (G,sigma) in terms of theta-null data.

evidence.quote: We denote by Mg(G, σ) be the sublocus in Mg of all the genus g curves X with G ,→ Aut (X ) and signature σ.
Problem 18. Describe the loci Mg(G, σ) in terms of the theta nulls for any given g, G, and σ.

accepted.question_text: For genus g >= 4, let G be an automorphism group of a genus-g curve and let M_g(G,sigma) be the locus of genus-g curves with automorphism group G and signature sigma. Describe this locus in terms of which theta-nulls vanish.

evidence.quote: We denote by Mg(G, σ) be the sublocus in Mg of all the genus g curves X with G ,→ Aut (X ) and signature σ.

Problem 19. Let G be an automorphism group of a genus Xg curve and Mg(G, σ) denote the locus of genus g curves with automorphism group G of some signature σ. For g >= 4, describe the locus Mg(G, σ) in terms of the vanishing theta-nulls.

accepted.question_text: Let k be a field and let phi:k^n -> k^m be a rational map with coordinate functions f_i=p_i(x)/q_i(x) of degrees d_i. Design an efficient algorithm, combining symbolic computation and numerical methods, to determine the degree of phi without relying solely on solving the generic polynomial system p_i(x)-y_i q_i(x)=0 by Groebner-basis computation.

evidence.quote: Let k be a field and φ : k n -> km be a rational map.
Problem 20. Combine the symbolic and numerical methods to design an efficient algorithm for determining the degree of a rational map.

accepted.question_text: Given a parametrizable algebraic surface X, design an efficient algorithm that finds a parametrization of X.

evidence.quote: There are no analogue results for higher dimensional varieties, even though there have been some attempts for algebraic surfaces.
Problem 21. Let X be a parametric algebraic surface. Design an algorithm which finds a parametrization of X .
